items.headline: Diner hit with undisclosed add-on charge, then pressured to tip
items.text: Nice atmosphere and friendly staff, but extremely disappointing experience. An expensive add-on was offered without clearly stating the price, only for me to discover the extra charge at the end. The add-on was even more expensive than the main course. Even high-end restaurants know better than to surprise customers with undisclosed charges. Being handed a tipping screen and pressured to tip on top of that was equally unclassy. Definitely not the experience you expect from a restaurant of this level. Wont be coming back.

items.headline: Family overcharged for baby amid half-hour chaotic check-in
items.text:
We had a rather disorganized experience at reception. The staff didn’t seem to know which tables were available and which were already occupied.

We visited with our two daughters, one almost 4 years old and the other 9 months old. We clearly explained that only our eldest daughter would be using the play area, as we first wanted to see whether the facilities were suitable for a 9-month-old baby.

The pricing is AED 90 for children aged 0–3 and AED 120 for children over 3. Despite explaining that only our eldest daughter would be using the play area, we were charged for both children: one at each price. To make matters even more confusing, the staff initially tried to give both children the wristband for the 0–3 age group. The whole process was extremely chaotic, with a clear lack of communication and organization.

In my opinion, the play area is not really suitable for a 9-month-old baby who is not yet walking.

After almost half an hour of confusion, another staff member stepped in and handled everything much more efficiently. She found us a table close to the play area and kindly refunded the extra charge. We really appreciated her help.

On a positive note, everyone was very friendly, and the venue itself is lovely and offers a great space for children to have fun. The food was average.

Overall, Nestt is a great place for families, but the reception process, communication and organization definitely need improvement. With a smoother check-in experience, it could be an even better place to visit.
items.author: Rocío Romero

items.headline: Birthday cake forgotten after 30-minute wait despite reservation
items.text:
A Very Disappointing Birthday Experience – Far Below Luxury Standards

I chose this restaurant to celebrate my birthday, expecting a special and memorable evening. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a deeply disappointing experience.

First of all, we had to wait 30 minutes for our table despite having a reservation. While I understand that Saturday evenings can be busy, what made the situation even more frustrating was the lack of space at the bar, leaving us standing around without even the possibility of enjoying a drink while waiting.

The service throughout the evening was equally disappointing. The first glass of wine I ordered was served with barely half the standard amount, which is simply unacceptable for a restaurant of this calibre.

However, the biggest disappointment came at the end of the dinner. Despite it being my birthday celebration, the staff completely forgot to bring out the birthday cake with the "Happy Birthday" message. A small but meaningful detail that should never be overlooked, especially when celebrating such an important occasion.

For a restaurant that presents itself as a luxury dining destination, the overall level of service was shockingly poor and nowhere near the standards one would expect.

I specifically chose this restaurant because I wanted my birthday to be special. Instead, the lack of attention to detail and poor service completely ruined an evening that meant a lot to me.

Luxury is not just about the atmosphere or the prices. It is about the experience, the attention to detail, and making guests feel valued. Unfortunately, this restaurant failed on all three.

Extremely disappointing, and certainly not an experience I would recommend for a special occasion.
items.author: Davide Parenza

items.headline: Guests surprised by AED 1,000 minimum spend after phone assurance
items.text:
⭐ 1/5 — Very Disappointing Experience at Billionaire Dubai

Very disappointing experience and extremely poor management.

I called Billionaire Dubai at 9:30 PM to ask if a reservation was required for two people. The staff clearly told me that no reservation was necessary. I also informed them that we would arrive at 10:00 PM.

However, when we arrived, we were suddenly informed that there was a minimum spend of AED 1,000 per person, and that all tables were fully booked.

Customers should be informed about such important conditions in advance, especially when they call ahead. They should not be surprised with a minimum spending requirement once they arrive at the entrance.

The issue is not the minimum spend itself, but the lack of communication, professionalism, and respect for customers’ time.

The way this situation was managed was completely unacceptable and reflects very poorly on the management.

For a venue with such a prestigious reputation, I expected much better organization, transparency, and customer service.

Very disappointing and definitely not the level of hospitality expected from a luxury venue in Dubai.
items.author: Haitham Abdulbaki

Also your food does not really taste like the Mumbai versions of the names you have given it.

I found a much better place in Al Nahda 1 at al Mattar tower behind Mai Tower, that is a hidden gem that gives really awesome Kadak Chai for AED 5 that is a full mug of very good tea. The atmosphere and the food is awesome too.

items.author: Roy

items.headline: Diner calls Power Lunch misleading, goes to McDonald's after
items.text:
Honestly, this was one of the worst steakhouse experiences I've ever had. I walked in expecting a decent meal, but walked out feeling like I'd been traumatized by the entire dining experience.

Let's start with the food. The salad was absolutely pathetic, the steak was nothing special (just basic and underwhelming), and the gravy was ridiculously salty.

Even the complimentary drinks served outside somehow managed to add to the trauma. At this point, I don't even know what to say anymore.

But what really made the experience worse was the so-called Power Lunch. Apparently, it's only available Monday to Friday, yet this restriction was nowhere clearly mentioned in their menu or advertised offer. That's seriously misleading. I genuinely felt scammed by the advertisement.

And here's the best part: after paying for and eating at a steakhouse, we actually ended up going straight to McDonald's because we were still unsatisfied.

To be fair, the servers were friendly and polite. They even asked us to leave a review, and well, here it is. Sorry, guys, but this is my honest feedback. Food-related misleading promotions and disappointing dining experiences shouldn't be normalized.

I've learned a good life lesson today:
"If it's too good to be true, it probably isn't true."

Imagine leaving a steakhouse and needing McDonald's to complete your meal!

Save your money and manage your expectations. You've been warned!⚠️⚠️⚠️
items.author: Ranj Guanco

items.headline: Birthday diner says rushed, inattentive service marred AED 800 dinner
items.text:
The restaurant is absolutely beautiful, very clean, and has a fantastic view. I genuinely loved the atmosphere, and the location is definitely worth visiting at least once.

However, there is something very important to mention: the entire management and restaurant operation, including the menu, changed on October 19. I took pictures of the current menu and uploaded them because most of the dishes shown in older customer reviews and photos are no longer available. Please keep this in mind when looking at previous reviews.

The food itself was delicious, and we were happy with everything we actually ordered. I also really appreciated the complimentary bread served with olive oil and balsamic vinegar, along with the tomato and cheese platter. Since it was my birthday, they surprised me with a complimentary cake and a candle. The cake was absolutely delicious, and that was a lovely gesture!

Unfortunately, the service was where the experience fell short. It took a very long time for the complimentary starters to arrive. While we were still trying to figure out the new menu, the waiters seemed more interested in clearing the table than allowing us to enjoy our meal. At one point, a waiter removed everything without even asking if we were finished. I hadn’t even had a chance to eat yet! After noticing my reaction, he asked if I wanted the food to stay. They eventually brought another plate of tomatoes and cheese, but the overall service felt rushed and unpleasant.

Another issue was the lack of consistent table service. Usually, at a restaurant of this level, one main server introduces themselves and takes care of your table throughout the evening. Here, different staff members kept coming to our table for every little thing: one for drinks, another for starters, and others for serving or clearing dishes. It felt like there were constantly people around our table, interrupting our conversations. We were a group of two , and honestly, we barely had a moment of privacy to relax and enjoy each other’s company.

There was also a lack of attention to detail and guidance when ordering. We asked for an eggplant dish, but they mistakenly brought us rice instead. By that point, we were so tired of the service that we didn’t even feel like pointing out the mistake. We also asked one of the waiters whether they served ribeye steak. He said he would check with the chef and get back to us, but he never came back with an answer. The staff also didn’t seem particularly interested in helping us understand the menu or recommending dishes.

It constantly felt like they wanted us to finish quickly and leave. Apparently, there is a two-to-two-and-a-half-hour time limit, but the restaurant was still open and most of the tables were empty. Considering that I spent around AED 800 that evening for a whole sea bass, sides, an appetizer, and two glasses of wine, I really expected a more relaxed and attentive dining experience.

There was also a female DJ playing music that I personally enjoyed, although music is always a matter of taste.

Overall, I loved the location, atmosphere, view, and food, but the service definitely affected the experience. The staff were not as attentive or welcoming as I would have expected from a restaurant at this price point. It’s a beautiful place with great potential, but the service, communication, and overall management need serious improvement.
items.author: Mia

items.headline: Cold welcome, small portions and loud music disappoint diner
items.text:
I rarely write negative reviews, and my intention here is not simply to criticise but to offer constructive feedback that might encourage the owners to improve the standards and reputation of their brand.

The restaurant certainly makes an impressive first impression. The building is beautiful, with striking architecture, luxurious décor, and ample parking. Clearly, considerable investment has gone into creating an attractive venue. Unfortunately, the quality of hospitality, service, and overall dining experience falls well short of what the surroundings promise.

First, the welcome. Upon arrival, the lady behind the reception monitor immediately began taking our details without a smile, a warm greeting, or any attempt to make us feel welcome. It felt more like checking into an administrative office than entering a premium restaurant.

Second, the seating arrangements. Without asking about our preferences or the purpose of our visit, we were escorted to a rather intimate, romantic seating area. I was dining with a female colleague, and the arrangement felt inappropriate and somewhat embarrassing. A simple question about seating preferences would have avoided this uncomfortable situation.

Third, the management and service. The manager approached our table and delivered what sounded like a rehearsed speech about the food, including an explanation of why a particular type of bread is placed beneath the kebab. There was no attempt to establish a conversation, engage with us, or understand our experience. Hospitality should be a dialogue, not a recorded presentation. Why I felt I am facing a robot rather than an experienced manager.

When I mentioned that my experience at the brand’s London restaurant had been rather different, he immediately insisted that both establishments were 100% identical. Rather than listening to a customer’s observation, he chose to contradict it. This is particularly concerning for a brand that presumably values consistency and reputation. Brand consistency should be demonstrated through the customer experience, not defended through argument.

Fourth, the food. The portions were disappointingly small, hardly sufficient for one person, particularly given the positioning of the restaurant. The dessert was equally underwhelming in flavour and presentation. While the staff appeared to be trying, enthusiasm alone cannot compensate for inadequate training and a lack of attention to detail. The temperature was cold and no arrangement to keep the food warm why having it or make the temperature a bit comfortable.

Finally, the atmosphere. Perhaps one of the most disappointing aspects was the music. It was excessively loud, with an almost party-like character, completely disconnected from the restaurant’s elegant architecture and supposedly refined dining environment. Combined with the dark and rather cold interior, it created an uncomfortable and confusing atmosphere. We found it difficult to relax and enjoy our meal.

My overall impression: This is a restaurant where substantial money has been invested in the building, interior design, and visual presentation, but seemingly far less attention has been given to the people, training, service culture, and actual dining experience.

Luxury is not defined by expensive decorations. It is defined by how customers are welcomed, understood, respected, and looked after.

I genuinely hope the owners take this feedback seriously. The venue has enormous potential, but without better hospitality standards, appropriate staff training, improved food quality, and a more thoughtfully managed atmosphere, the impressive surroundings alone will not sustain the reputation of the brand.

A beautiful restaurant, unfortunately, does not automatically make a good restaurant.
items.author: Ehsan Daneshvar

items.headline: Steak served raw, then replacement came back burned and dry
items.text:
Unfortunately, what was supposed to be a great dining experience turned into a very disappointing one.

We specifically requested our steak medium well , but what we received was practically raw (as shown in the pictures below). When we raised the issue and asked for it to be corrected, the replacement was completely overcooked, burned, dry, and tasteless. It honestly felt like they had simply reheated it and brought it back to the table without any care or attention to quality.

To make matters worse, the service was just as disappointing as the food. The staff kept ignoring our concerns, and whenever we tried to get someone to take responsibility, they kept pointing us toward other staff members instead of actually helping us resolve the issue. There was no proper communication, ownership, or willingness to make things right.

The only positive thing about this place is the view, which is genuinely beautiful. Unfortunately, a nice view cannot make up for poor food quality and terrible service.

Overall, a very disappointing experience. We came expecting a good meal and left feeling frustrated and dissatisfied. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and pays more attention to both food quality and customer service.

The pictures below speak for themselves

items.headline: Guard calls linen trousers sportswear; dark, deafening dining room
items.text:
We visited Tattu Dubai today as a party of four, having booked a table in advance for 7:45 PM.

Let me start with the positives: the food was genuinely delicious. The beef gyoza were absolutely outstanding, as were the duck and watermelon salad, miso salmon, and chocolate fondant. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Having visited over 30 countries and dined at hundreds of restaurants, I can honestly say I’ve rarely experienced such an unpleasant attitude towards guests. And we’re not demanding customers — we don’t expect anyone to fuss over us. Just take our order, bring our food, and let us enjoy our evening.

The experience started in the lobby, where an arrogant security guard insisted that my husband’s grey linen trousers were “sportswear” and refused to let us in unless we were hotel guests. Meanwhile, another man wearing shorts was allowed through without any issues. Thankfully, the lovely reception women explained that linen trousers are not sportswear, and we were finally allowed in.

Things only got worse upstairs. The restaurant is so dark that you literally cannot read the menu without your phone’s flashlight. The music is deafening — you can barely hear the waiter, your companions, or even yourself. It feels more like a badly managed nightclub than an upscale restaurant.

Almost none of the non-alcoholic drinks on the menu were available, so we ended up ordering water and Sprite. The “Inauguration” cocktail, costing nearly €20, tasted like water mixed with jam.

We waited around 30 minutes just for the waiter to take our order. To be fair, the restaurant was extremely busy, so I suspect this was more of a staffing issue than the waiter’s fault.

And don’t expect spectacular views. The panoramic windows are so dirty and cloudy that you can barely see anything through them. Ironically, the view from the ladies’ restroom is fantastic — and the windows there are perfectly clean!

Interestingly, the bar area is much more pleasant: brighter lighting, significantly quieter music, and a far more enjoyable atmosphere. Unfortunately, the restaurant itself is a complete disappointment.

Final verdict: excellent food cannot compensate for terrible organization, an uncomfortable atmosphere, and such poor treatment of guests. No matter how good the food is, we will never return.
items.author: Евгения Михайлова

items.headline: AED 490 launch brunch served no mains, not even water
items.text:
Ladybird Brunch – Not Worth the Price

We paid AED 490 per person for the brunch, and honestly, the experience was extremely disappointing, especially considering the price.

For a table of five, we were served two sets of starters, including pizza, guacamole, chicken popcorn, lentil salad, kale salad, cheese, and two small pizzas. No main courses were served at all.

We were then offered two desserts and three drinks per person. Even water was not included!

For AED 490 per person, I expected a much better selection of food, proper main courses, and an overall experience that justified the price. Unfortunately, none of that was delivered.

I have never felt so underwhelmed by a brunch experience, especially one at this price point. What makes it even more disappointing is that this was the launch of the brunch.

Overall, definitely not worth AED 490 per person. I would not recommend it.
items.author: ines bousnina
